notes:
Summary: evaluation for Dedicated capacity focused on low-latency reranking and customer chat for maritime operations.

Key contacts: CTO - Marta Li; Product lead - Omar Hines. AE: Sofia Martinez. SE: Daniel Cho. CSM: Priya Desai.

Business drivers / why now:
- Live routing + chat across ships: must reduce human handling and speed up ETA adjustments.
- High QPS for short responses (reranking + chat snippets); currently hitting rate limits on managed FaaS.
- Cost predictability important for annual contract procurement.

POC scope (what Redwood will demonstrate):
- Dedicated pool provisioned (8xA100 equiv) with routing policy to fallback model small-quantized on overload.
- Performance bench: open-loop load tests to measure sustained throughput; closed-loop latency under target load; 72-hour soak test to validate stability and memory leaks.
- Representative workloads: reranking (top-20 -> top-5), chat (multi-turn, avg 60 tokens), embeddings (batch 128), real-time routing inference (short 12-24 token outputs).
- Acceptance criteria: sustained 250 requests/sec for reranking pipeline (avg 3K tokens/sec), p95 latency <=150ms for chat single-token streaming, error rate <0.1%, no OOMs during 72h soak.

Performance targets and constraints discussed on call:
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for representative prompts.
- Throughput: target 200-300 rps for reranking (depending on model), peak burst up to 600 rps for short windows.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask 8 GPUs (customer preference M60-class equiv) with option to scale to 16 if soak shows CPU/GPU utilization high.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to trade perf for quantization if unit cost reduces by >=25%.

Technical notes from SE workshop (Daniel):
- Model candidates: open-weights Llama-derivative (quantized 4-bit) and a medium-sized distilled model for fallback.
- Batching strategy: adaptive batching with max-delay 15ms; target batch size 8-12 for reranking path.
- KV-cache reuse expected for chat sessions; need sticky routing and session affinity.
- Disk-backed KV cache considered for long conversations to limit memory footprint during soak.

Tests planned / timeline:
- 2026-02-18: kickoff demo call (FF-20260218-quantum-anchorage-demo) -> initial perf numbers captured.
- 2026-02-25: prelim open-loop load test (single-model, synthetic prompts) -> passed baseline but high tail latency under bursts.
- 2026-03-01: configuration change (batching + kernel switch) deployed to staging; rerun smoke.
- 2026-03-05: start 72h soak across two model variants (quantized small + distilled medium). Monitoring dashboards shared.
- 2026-03-12: POC report due; include cost projection, SLA wording suggestions, recommended reserved GPU count.

Security & compliance:
- Completed initial security questionnaire; SOC2 and ISO questions flagged around tenant isolation for VPC.
- Legal asks: explicit SLA credits for sustained p95 violations over 24h; finance wants term sheet showing rollback to hosted API rate limits as fallback.

Negotiation points / commercial:
- Customer wants 12-month reserved capacity with monthly billing cadence; negotiating buffer burst credits and failure credits.
- Want explicit SLOs for latency and throughput in contract. Legal pushing for 30% cap on outage credit; Redwood legal proposing 10%.

Open action items:
- SE to provide exact GPU utilization graphs from staging (Daniel) by 2026-03-07.
- Solutions to draft fallback routing flow for on-price/latency tradeoffs (Sofia + Daniel).
- Sales to get procurement docs and internal PO workflow; customer to share procurement deadline (end of April).

Misc fragments / quotes from calls:
- "We need predictable latency for port-side automation, otherwise operators won't trust it" - Marta Li (CTO).
- "If you can show 72 hours with no memory growth we can sign" - Omar Hines (Product).

Next steps (short):
- Finish soak, collate logs, deliver POC report with recommended reserved GPUs and expected monthly run-rate.
- Legal to align SLA credit language and confirm VPC tenant isolation diagram.
